title: Prosecutors preparing for VP showdown
summary: Preparing for a potential showdown with Vice President Sara Duterte at her impeachment trial, the House prosecution panel said it is ready to cross-examine her should she decide to take the witness…

blocks.text: Women lawyers in the prosecution panel include (clockwise from left) Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro, San Juan Rep. Ysabel Zamora and private prosecutors Mae Divinagracia and Lorna Kapunan. Manila Rep. Joel Chua said a female lawyer will grill the Vice President in case she decides to take the witness stand.

MANILA, Philippines — Preparing for a potential showdown with Vice President Sara Duterte at her impeachment trial, the House prosecution panel said it is ready to cross-examine her should she decide to take the witness stand.

House prosecutor and Manila 3rd district Rep. Joel Chua said they are looking at three scenarios in the defense strategy, one of which is the Vice President herself appearing as a “surprise witness” at her trial.
With only two witnesses for four trial dates this week, Chua said they are looking at the possibility that Duterte’s lawyers would let her take the witness stand.
“The panel of prosecutors is ready in case our Vice President appears as witness for the defense,” he said at a weekly forum in Quezon City yesterday.
Chua said they have already assigned one of their lawyers who will cross-examine Duterte in case she decides to attend hearings. He said the lawyer is a woman but declined to identify her.
Duterte said on Friday that she had wanted to lawyer for herself but her lead counsel Michael Poa seemed averse to her proposal.

“He does not acknowledge it. Somehow, he changes the subject,” Duterte claimed. In another scenario, the defense may seek another postponement, or rest her case altogether after presenting two to three witnesses.

Duterte’s legal team is set to present two witnesses: Lourdes Lebosada, the alleged business partner of her husband Manases Carpio in Cale88 Foods Corp, and Bureau of Customs deputy commissioner for assessment and operations coordinating group Agaton Teodoro Uvero.
Chua said Agaton would likely present documents of exportation of Cale88 while Lebosada would testify about the operations of the banana chips firm.
The House prosecutor also appealed to the court to call out the defense’s delaying tactics, such as requests for postponement of trial dates.
“We are seeing that the presiding officer is quite lax with them,” Chua said.
While hinting at her possible attendance during the last few trial days, Duterte said she cannot guarantee her physical presence at the Senate on the day of verdict.
“It depends. If I am in Davao, then no, because we have a series of activities for the Davao Thanksgiving this December,” she said.

“We are always preparing for the worst because if there is an acquittal, it will just be a continuation of what we are doing now for the Office of the Vice President. So next year, all the projects and all the programs would be implemented,” Duterte noted.
In case of a conviction, the Vice President said she is also considering her options, such as engaging in child abuse prevention projects or being a full-time mother to her children.

“I have confidence in the Lord’s plan in all these things happening in my life. But I am not confident in the Lord’s plan for the Philippines. So, it is scary what His plans are for the country,” she said. — Evelyn Macairan, Daphne Galvez
